# Muse Memory

> Autonomous, local-first cognitive memory engine for AI coding agents and agency networks. Runs in-process: sub-2ms recall, write-time citation verification, 52 agent platforms wired by one command, 0 background daemons, MIT licensed.
>
> Version 3.3.0 · https://harshsinghmp.github.io/musememory/

Muse Memory gives an AI agent a memory that survives between sessions. Every memory is checked against the real code before it is stored and re-checked before it is served, so an agent is never handed a fact that has since become false.

## Install

```bash
npx musememory connect
```

No account, no API key, no configuration file, no background daemon. The store is two plain directories: `.memory/` inside each project and `~/.memory/` globally.

## Authoritative machine-readable files

- [`claims.json`](claims.json) — every countable figure, generated from `src/`.
- [`docs/mcp-tool-matrix.json`](docs/mcp-tool-matrix.json) — the registered MCP tool list, generated.
- [`schema.json`](schema.json) — the memory entry schema.

Never hand-edit these three; regenerate with `bun run claims:generate`.

## Key entry points

- `src/` — engine source (CLI, MCP server, store, retrieval, cognition).
- `bin/` — `memory` / `musememory` executables.
- `test/` — Bun test suite (`bun test`).
- `apps/website/` — the Astro site published at `/musememory`.
- `.agents/` — agent standards, durable context and terrain maps.

## MCP tools an agent should know

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `get_context` | Mandatory on the first turn of a session. Fused recall: constraints, ranked memories, negative lessons, code anchors, under one token budget. |
| `memory_capture` | Persist a decision, fix or constraint. Every write is secret-scanned and citation-verified. |
| `search` | Full-text search across the store. |
| `memory_current` | Read or write the active working constraints in CURRENT.md. |
| `muse_context` | Task-shaped fused context for a specific job. |
| `muse_why` | Explain why the code is the way it is, from ADRs and past fixes. |
| `memory_supersede` | Replace an outdated memory with a newer one. |

126 tools are registered in total, exposed through 7 task-focused profiles (`core`, `coding`, `debugging`, `review`, `architecture`, `maintenance`, `full`).

## Behaviour an agent must know

1. Call `get_context` on the first turn of any session.
2. Capture decisions, fixes and constraints as they happen — `memory_capture`.
3. Supersede rather than delete when knowledge changes — `memory_supersede`.
4. Every write is scanned for credentials and refused if one is present.
5. Every code citation is verified against the live filesystem at write time and re-checked at recall; drifted memories are withheld and reported, not served.
